events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Crowned Emperor of the French
events.description: At Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, Napoleon crowned himself emperor in a ceremony attended by Pope Pius VII, then crowned his wife Joséphine as empress. Taking the crown from the Pope's hands and placing it on his own head symbolized that his power derived from himself rather than the Church.
events.significance: Marked the formal transition from the French Republic to the First French Empire and ushered in the Napoleonic era, which reshaped European politics, law, and warfare.

events.title: President James Monroe Announces the Monroe Doctrine
events.description: In his annual message to Congress, President James Monroe declared that the Western Hemisphere was closed to further European colonization and that US would view European interference in the Americas as hostile acts. In return, the US pledged not to interfere in European affairs or existing colonies.
events.significance: Became a cornerstone of US foreign policy for nearly two centuries, shaping American relations with Latin America and Europe.

events.title: Abolitionist John Brown Executed
events.description: John Brown was hanged in Charles Town, Virginia, after being convicted of treason, murder, and inciting a slave insurrection following his October 1859 raid on the federal armory at Harpers Ferry.
events.significance: Brown's execution deepened the sectional divide between North and South and made him a martyr for abolitionists, helping set the stage for the American Civil War.

events.title: First Controlled Nuclear Chain Reaction
events.description: A team led by Enrico Fermi achieved the first self-sustaining, controlled nuclear chain reaction in Chicago Pile-1, a reactor built beneath the stands of Stagg Field at the University of Chicago, as part of the Manhattan Project.
events.significance: Demonstrated the feasibility of harnessing nuclear energy, paving the way for both nuclear weapons and nuclear power.

events.title: First Permanent Artificial Heart Implanted
events.description: Surgeons at the University of Utah led by William DeVries implanted the Jarvik-7 artificial heart into retired dentist Barney Clark, who survived 112 days with the device.
events.significance: A landmark in cardiac medicine that advanced research into mechanical circulatory support and later heart-assist technologies.
